summary:
ARES (Astronaut Reconnaissance Exploration System) is an offline-first surface navigation and safety platform for human Marswalks, solving the critical challenges of zero GPS infrastructure, hazardous terrain slopes exceeding 15°, and a 20-minute communication latency from Earth. 

  ARES integrates official USGS Mars 2020 HiRISE DTM mosaics, NASA Mars Trek topography, University of Arizona imagery (ESP_090619_1985), JPL 3D rover assets, and MEDA weather baselines. Running a localized A* pathfinding engine directly in the browser, the system continuously analyzes slope safety limits, projects real-time dynamic guidance on a unified 3D HUD, and automates autonomous rover recall ("Summon Rover") to park a support vehicle at a 4-meter standoff. It also structures geological field science waypoints like Cheyava Falls to unlock PIXL and SHERLOC mineral data.  

 To bypass the fatal limitation of touchscreens in pressurized EVA gloves, ARES features a custom hardware-software integration console powered by an Arduino Uno, analog joysticks, status LEDs, and an LCD display connected via a serial bridge for zero-latency tactile control and voice copilot queries.
details:
On Mars, a single wrong turn is fatal. When human astronauts step outside their habitat on an Extravehicular Activity (EVA), they enter one of the most unforgiving environments in the solar system—completely stripped of the safety nets we take for granted on Earth. There is zero GPS infrastructure, no cellular network, and no real-time satellite positioning. The Martian terrain is deceptive and treacherous, filled with loose regolith, hidden crater rims, and steep inclines exceeding the critical 15-degree threshold where bulky, pressurized spacesuits lose traction and stability. Worse still, a 20-minute radio communication latency between Mars and Earth means Mission Control cannot guide explorers step-by-step in real time. Once an astronaut steps onto the Martian surface, survival depends entirely on local, autonomous intelligence—and hardware that actually works through thick, pressurized EVA gloves.

To solve this, we engineered ARES — the Astronaut Reconnaissance Exploration System, an offline-first, full-stack surface navigation, hazard-avoidance, and rover-coordination platform designed specifically for human Marswalks. Rather than building a passive 3D map viewer, we built an active life-support and tactical guidance partner that bridges orbital planetary science with surface-level human survival.

Here is how ARES transforms Martian surface exploration:

  • We ground navigation in real planetary science: We reconstruct authentic Martian surface environments around Jezero Crater, Bright Angel, and Cheyava Falls using official USGS Mars 2020 HiRISE Digital Terrain Model (DTM) mosaics, NASA Mars Trek topography, University of Arizona HiRISE orbital imagery (ESP_090619_1985), JPL-Caltech 3D rover assets, and Perseverance MEDA environmental baselines.
  • We enforce real-time slope and hazard safety: ARES runs a local A* pathfinding engine directly in the browser with zero cloud dependency. It continuously evaluates terrain gradients, strictly blocking routes steeper than 15.0 degrees, projecting dynamic ground-level navigation vectors on a unified 3D Heads-Up Display (HUD), and triggering tiered CLEAR, CAUTION, and HALT proximity advisories before an astronaut steps into danger.
  • We automate autonomous rover support: Astronauts shouldn't have to haul heavy instruments across hazardous regolith. With a single command, ARES coordinates an independent Perseverance support rover to calculate its own safe A* corridor and park at a precise 4-meter standoff beside the explorer.
  • We streamline field science discovery: ARES guides astronauts through structured geological waypoints, automatically unlocking interactive PIXL and SHERLOC mineralogical spectrometry records upon arrival at key targets like Cheyava Falls.
  • We engineered physical, glove-friendly hardware integration: Because capacitive touchscreens fail in pressurized spacesuits, we paired our software with a custom physical command console powered by an Arduino Uno, a breadboard circuit, tactile analog joysticks, high-visibility status LEDs, and a real-time LCD telemetry readout connected via a serial bridge—alongside a hands-free voice copilot.

ARES turns raw orbital data into immediate, intuitive surface survival—giving future explorers the confidence to navigate the Red Planet safely, autonomously, and tactically.
